messages:
incident-bot: SEV-1 alert: Dedicated pool 'orchid-dedicated-42' node orchid-42-3 is flapping GPUs; several tenant connections (dedicated tenants) reported errors and elevated tail latency. Pager: sre_oncall. Impact: some requests to HelixLabs VPC models are failing or timing out.

sre_oncall: Ack. I see increasing 5xx from model-router for that pool. Triage in-flight. Any idea if this is hardware or infra?

compute_oncall: I'm pulling node metrics. GPU0 shows ECC spikes and NVLink errors. Kernel logs show PCIe reset events. Possible NVLink fabric issue.

reliability_lead: Tagging for reliability: @compute_oncall please confirm whether this is causing corrupted inferences or only timeouts. We need to decide tenant isolation ASAP.

compute_oncall: So far it's mostly requests failing with `gpu-device-reset` and `CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN`. No signs of token-level corruption in logs, just resets mid-generation. I'd treat as availability impact only.

eng_infra: If it's device resets we should cordon and drain node orchid-42-3, move tenants off, and mark for replacement. Can we do rolling drain without a larger outage?

infra_pm: Approving drain. Is there capacity in the dedicated pool to absorb HelixLabs traffic? If not, we need to route to their fallback (hosted variant) and notify account team.

account_eng: HelixLabs is on dedicated SLA. We must avoid model quality regression. Recommend: failover only to a pinned compatible hosted variant with exact model version, limit throughput, and inform them. I'll prep a message.

compute_oncall: Steps I propose: 1) cordon orchid-42-3 2) evict workloads 3) enable emergency routing for HelixLabs to hosted fallback 4) mark node degraded and schedule replacement. Doable now.

sre_oncall: Do it. Start with cordon/drain. Include `deploy-bot` to run drain jobs so we have audit trail.

deploy-bot: Running drain job: `drain-orchid-node --node orchid-42-3 --timeout 15m --force-evict`

compute_oncall: Drain started. Eviction progress: 4/8 tenant instances evicted, 2 stuck in termination due to long-running KV cache flush.

eng_infra: For stuck pods, we'll push `SIGTERM` then `SIGKILL` after 30s. KV cache will be warm on fallback; ensure cache priming for the hosted fallback.

reliability_lead: @eng_infra coordinate cache priming. Low latency requests first, then background prefetch. We don't want cold-start blips.

eng_infra: Starting cache priming for HelixLabs model variants on hosted pool. Script: 
```
priming-cli --tenant helixlabs --model v3.1 --pattern small-samples --parallel 6
```
Estimated 3-4 minutes.

compute_oncall: Evictions complete. Node cordoned. All HelixLabs traffic now being routed to hosted fallback. Verified model outputs matching on sample prompts.

account_eng: Draft message to customer sent to private channel for review: "We're experiencing a dedicated GPU node failure in your reserved pool. We've routed your traffic to a verified hosted fallback with the same model version to avoid quality regression. Our team is replacing the faulty node and will provide ETA within 2 hours. No data was exfiltrated." Any edits?

reliability_lead: Good. Add note about possible brief latency increase while priming, and that we'll provide an incident postmortem.

account_eng: Updated and sent. Customer acknowledged with :thumbsup:. They asked for a rough ETA for node replacement.

infra_pm: Engage hardware replacement: @eng_infra please confirm spare node availability in region and whether replacement requires maintenance window.

eng_infra: Spare capacity available. Replacement procedure: schedule physical host reprovision (replace GPU board if NVLink fabric defective), reprovision OS, join pool. Estimate 90–120 minutes for full replacement and validation.

compute_oncall: I'll keep the node cordoned and mark `orchid-42-3` as `degraded->drain-replace`. Added to incident tracker.

deploy-bot: Audit note: orchid-42-3: cordon at 2065004387, drain complete at 2065004560, marked degraded.

incident-bot: Incident updated to SEV-1 (Tenant impact) — status: mitigation in place (traffic rerouted) — next update ETA 30m.

sre_oncall: Handoff to midnight oncall in 45m. @compute_oncall continue replacement steps; @reliability_lead please own postmortem; @account_eng maintain customer comms. If we see further pool-wide flapping, escalate to infra PM for capacity rebalancing.

compute_oncall: Accepted. I'll trigger hardware replacement now and monitor for any other nodes showing similar PCIe/AER patterns.

eng_infra: Replacement task created: ticket INFRA-78321. GPU board flagged for return. Will update when host back in service.

reliability_lead: Note for postmortem: collect dmesg, NVLink logs, kernel AER dumps, and recent driver rollout history. We should check if a driver update rolled last week to this pool.

sre_oncall: Also check our autoscale throttle logs — ensure we didn't block capacity expansion during mitigation.

incident-bot: Paging summary sent to #incidents: 2065004321. Next update will include replacement ETA and any additional affected tenants.

compute_oncall: Quick log excerpt: 
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.568000] pcieport 0000:63:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Fatal) error received: id=00e0
[ 1234.568100] GPU0: PCIe AER: Uncorrectable error, device reset
```
Cause still under investigation (hardware vs firmware).

account_eng: Customer asked if we can route non-critical batch jobs to hosted pool permanently until replacement — they worry about user-facing consistency. I recommended routing only real-time traffic to hosted fallback and keeping batch on dedicated if that's acceptable. They agreed to that temporary split.

reliability_lead: Good trade-off. Documenting mitigation choices. We'll include traffic split in postmortem timeline.

sre_oncall: Marking incident as active-mitigated; handoff note: midnight team to validate replacement progress and confirm node rejoin or reprovision. Last update 2065007850.

incident-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026-042 created and linked to INFRA-78321 and postmortem stub.

compute_oncall: I'll post final status when host replaced or if pattern emerges across nodes.

eng_infra: For now, node orchid-42-3 remains out of rotation. Replacement ETA 100 minutes.

account_eng: Customer thanked team and asked for ping once node is back. I'll follow up. :pray:
